title: Wording of X-Frame-Options as legacy and "obseleted"
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

Currently [the spec](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#x-frame-options) has the following (emphasis my own):

> The `X-Frame-Options` HTTP response header is a **legacy way** of controlling whether and how a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) may be loaded inside of a [child navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#child-navigable). It is **obsoleted by the [frame-ancestors](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors) CSP directive**, which provides more granular control over the same situations. It was originally defined in HTTP Header Field X-Frame-Options, but the definition and processing model here supersedes that document. [[CSP]](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/references.html#refsCSP) [[RFC7034]](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/references.html#refsRFC7034)

That wording has been taken to mean that [`X-Frame-Options` is deprecated and should be discouraged](https://github.com/mdn/browser-compat-data/pull/25663). That is not the case.

`X-Frame-Options` is limited (and in particular the `ALLOW-FROM` variant is poorly supported and that is unlikely to change. CSP does offer a better solution to that use case.

However, outside of that, the use of `X-Frame-Options` is well supported and is unlikely to be removed from browsers (without causing a massive degradation in security for no real benefit). This is especially true as [CSP usage considerably trails `X-Frame-Options`](https://almanac.httparchive.org/en/2024/security#fig-31) (and [only half of those use `frame-ancestors`](https://almanac.httparchive.org/en/2024/security#fig-16)!)

I suggest a new wording of (again emphasis my own - and this emphasis wouldn't be included in the spec and is only shown here to show the changes):

> The `X-Frame-Options` HTTP response header is **an older** way of controlling whether and how a [Document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/dom.html#document) may be loaded inside of a [child navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#child-navigable). **For sites using CSP, the [`frame-ancestors`](https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-csp/#frame-ancestors) CSP directive** provides more granular control over the same situations. `X-Frame-Options` was originally defined in HTTP Header Field X-Frame-Options, but the definition and processing model here supersedes that document. [[CSP]](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/references.html#refsCSP) [[RFC7034]](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/references.html#refsRFC7034)

WDYT?
